reason: The low test tether should keep the first flight contained; it is also the only offered action.
expectation: I expect to secure the whale for its low lift test, though the balance and landing still need attention.

effect: The whale is tethered; the padded landing cradle is the next available preparation.
reaction: A sensible safety step, though the result gives little detail.
reason: The cradle should protect the whale during its low test, and it is the only offered gameplay action.
expectation: I expect the cradle to provide a padded landing beneath the tethered whale.

effect: The whale now has a padded landing area for the test.
reaction: The safety preparations make sense, though they are sequential and predictable.
reason: The lift-control lead is the only offered gameplay action and should let me control the test.
expectation: I expect to connect the lift controls so the whale can be raised and lowered during the test.

effect: The lift works, but the dragon end is too heavy, so the whale needs rebalancing before another test.
reaction: The uneven load is a useful, concrete problem after the predictable safety preparations.
reason: The counterweight handle is the only offered gameplay action and should help balance the nose-heavy whale.
expectation: I expect to shift the counterweight away from the heavy dragon end, though a further test may be needed to check the balance.

effect: The counterweight adjustment has rebalanced the whale, but its level still needs checking.
reaction: The adjustment addresses the tilt, though the result gives no detail about how it was moved.
reason: The bubble level is the only offered gameplay action and should check the balance.
expectation: I expect to check whether the whale hangs level, possibly with another lift test.

effect: The level confirms that the counterweight adjustment lets the whale hover evenly on its tether.
reaction: Satisfying to see an ordinary balancing mechanism solve the flying whale's tilt.
reason: The stop cord is the only offered gameplay action and should provide a way to stop the lift.
expectation: I expect the cord and lever to operate the exterior stop button and bring the whale down gently.

effect: The stop cord cuts lift immediately; a gentle landing instead requires gradually reducing current. The chapter is complete.
reaction: The distinction between an emergency stop and a controlled landing was a useful clarification.

mostWorthwhile.text: Finding the nose-heavy hover and correcting it made the balance problem concrete; checking it with the bubble level gave the adjustment a satisfying result.

leastWorthwhile.text: The tether and padded landing preparations were sensible but predictable, with only one gameplay action offered at each step.

surprise.text: The emergency stop cuts lift immediately rather than landing the whale gently; the controller is needed for a gradual descent.

arbitrary.text: No action felt purposeless, though the counterweight result did not explain how it was moved.

continue.text: I would be curious to continue and see the fair in use, especially after the balancing test, though the mostly forced sequence makes me less eager for more assembly.
